purpose: Reconcile archived 54-lesson sequence and duplicate open 55-lesson proposal without overwriting any historical ID or creating a second doctrinal Q&A.

authority.catechism: Existing published 433-question St Pius X corpus owns the Q&A

governance: The original 54 lesson IDs are permanent archival reference IDs, not overwritten by the proposed 55-title teaching order.
New Precepts subject at display LTF-046 is an explicitly authored candidate; original historical LTF-046 remains 'What prayer is' and maps to proposed display LTF-047.
Each numbered Catechism question has one primary teaching lesson, verified 433/433; other lessons may link to it by reference without becoming additional Q&A copies.
Mass, sacraments, morality, Spiritual Life, prayer, liturgical year are distinct existing owners; preserve cross-links, don't duplicate practice or live rites.
The two older standalone 55-lesson PRs #490/#495 are alternative witnesses, not additional modules; don't merge both.
No lesson can become public before independent claim-level source/theological verification and native-French editorial approval.

teachingClaims.en: The precepts of the Church concretize duties of worship, sacramental life, penance and support of the Church under legitimate ecclesiastical authority.
teachingClaims.fr: Les préceptes de l’Église concrétisent les devoirs de culte, de vie sacramentelle, de pénitence et de soutien de l’Église sous l’autorité ecclésiastique légitime.

sourceScopeDeskReview.sourcePassageComparison: 1912 Italian legge-precetti.md Q213–226 read in full

teachingClaims.en: Fasting and abstinence express the Church’s authority to prescribe communal penance, but the detailed ages, days and forms found in the 1912 catechism belong to historical discipline and must not be presented as current universal law.
teachingClaims.fr: Le jeûne et l’abstinence expriment l’autorité de l’Église pour prescrire une pénitence commune, mais les âges, jours et formes détaillés du catéchisme de 1912 relèvent d’une discipline historique et ne doivent pas être présentés comme le droit universel actuel.

sourceScopeDeskReview.sourcePassageComparison: 1912 Italian legge-precetti.md Q213–226 read in full

teachingClaims.en: The 1912 Italian Catechism describes a restriction on the nuptial Mass and special blessing from the First Sunday of Advent to Christmas and from Ash Wednesday to Easter Sunday. The authorized 1913 French printing gives the periods as Advent to Epiphany and the beginning of Lent to the octave of Easter. Both describe historical ceremonial restrictions, not conditions for valid matrimonial consent.
teachingClaims.fr: Le catéchisme italien de 1912 décrit une restriction de la messe nuptiale et de la bénédiction spéciale des époux du premier dimanche de l’Avent à Noël et du mercredi des Cendres au dimanche de Pâques. L’édition française autorisée de 1913 indique de l’Avent à l’Épiphanie et du début du Carême à l’octave de Pâques. Ces règles historiques concernent la célébration rituelle, non la validité du consentement matrimonial.
